update_frequency: Scheduled approximately every 3 hours; manual workflow runs are also supported
source_note: Updates are summarized from recent reports. Allegations are attributed and are not treated as proven. Use official APSEC orders for final legal status.

items.title: APSEC reopens nominations in four urban local bodies
items.summary: On 22 October, the Andhra Pradesh State Election Commission reportedly extended nominations for 48 hours on 23 and 24 October, from 11 AM to 3 PM, in Kadapa Municipal Corporation, Rajampet Municipality, Mydukuru Municipality and Tirupati Municipal Corporation. The decision followed Supreme Court directions and complaints that some candidates were prevented from filing papers. The SEC's revised schedule reports the final candidate list for 25 October, polling on 1 November, repoll if required on 2 November, and counting on 3 November. Confirm the signed APSEC notification before relying on the dates.
items.note: Summary of media report; check APSEC's original order for authoritative details.

items.title: Revised municipal election schedule after Supreme Court directions
items.summary: Reporting says the SEC revised the timetable for the 100 urban local bodies after the Supreme Court directed it to examine complaints and consider extensions where candidates were allegedly blocked from filing nominations. The four bodies receiving an additional nomination window are in Kadapa and Tirupati districts; the revised schedule says polling is 1 November and counting 3 November. The earlier 28 October date should not be relied on without checking the revised official notice.
items.note: Court directions and reported SEC action; official notification remains controlling.

items.title: YSRCP alleges 76 incidents during MPTC/ZPTC nomination period
items.summary: YSRCP state coordinator Sajjala Ramakrishna Reddy alleged 76 incidents across 11 districts, including threats, confinement, attacks and destruction of nomination papers. The party said 22 incidents were in YSR Kadapa, 18 in Palnadu, and 11 each in Annamayya and Tirupati, with the remainder across seven other districts. These figures are the party's claim, not an independently verified total; TDP rejected the allegations and made counterclaims.
items.note: Both the allegation and the counterclaim should be checked against police / SEC records as they become available.

items.title: Kadapa MP Avinash Reddy taken into preventive custody during nominations
items.summary: The Indian Express reported that police took YSRCP MP Y.S. Avinash Reddy into preventive custody near the party office in Kadapa as MPTC/ZPTC nominations began; the report says he was taken away to prevent possible clashes and that other party leaders were also placed under house arrest. YSRCP criticised the action and alleged its candidates were being obstructed. Police action and the party's interpretation are distinct claims; seek official police details for the stated legal grounds.
items.status: Police action reported; political claims disputed
items.note: Report-based summary, not a finding that any party committed wrongdoing.

items.title: Supreme Court review triggered by nomination-obstruction complaints
items.summary: Recent reporting says the Supreme Court directed APSEC to defer publication of final candidate lists and examine representations and supporting evidence, including electronic evidence, where candidates alleged they were prevented from filing nominations because of law-and-order problems. The SEC initially halted further proceedings across all 100 urban local bodies, then announced a 48-hour nomination extension in four ULBs. The matter was reported for further court consideration on 27 October.
items.note: Check the latest court order and APSEC notification for current status.

items.title: MPTC/ZPTC nominations continue amid reports of house arrests and complaints
items.summary: South First reported that YSRCP alleged several leaders were placed under house arrest during MPTC/ZPTC nominations and that candidates were being prevented from filing papers. The report says Avinash Reddy was later released after being taken into custody. These are reported party allegations and police actions; the article includes the party's statements, not an independent finding that the allegations are proven.
items.note: Claims require verification against police and election-authority records.
